sources.title: Temple of Hercules Victor · Wikipedia
sources.citation: Direct text review: peripteral tholos, 20 Corinthian columns (19 survive), 14.8 m overall diameter, column height 10.65 m, later 2nd c. BC date, point coordinate 41.88861 N 12.48083 E (rounded). Secondary source; figures corroborated by World History Encyclopedia.

sources.title: Temple of Vesta/Hercules, Rome · World History Encyclopedia
sources.citation: Direct text review: five-step tufa base, Pentelic marble, 1st c. AD column replacements, dimensions agreeing with Wikipedia.

sources.citation: Public domain by age; the scan carries no stated licence. Plan ratios measured by eye (cella/colonnade ~0.645, wall ~0.073); Palladio draws about 12 columns, not 20, and a dome; both rejected. No image pixels used.

evidence.note: City visitor point adopted as a model discovery anchor, with unquantified positional accuracy. Not a surveyed footprint.
Named Roman temple. Pleiades dates it to the late 2nd or early 1st century BC; the date range here is approximate and encodes no unchanged appearance.

Derived, not surveyed: the Portunus visitor anchor plus the vector (-11.6 m east, 56.6 m south) between the two OpenStreetMap temple outlines, whose stated accuracy is 20 m. The earlier rounded Wikipedia point (41.88861 N, 12.48083 E) lies about 20 m away from the OpenStreetMap outline centre and was not used.
Named Roman temple, standing, dated to the later 2nd century BC. Peripteral tholos of 20 Corinthian columns.

Combines two separately reviewed exterior interpretations. Their relative placement is approximate; extent and foundation rise are renderer limits. The preview date is editorial, not a verified state.
